column1: In the Microsoft Learn VS Code workflow, switch to {{c1::Agent}} mode so Copilot can invoke configured MCP tools.
column2:
Agent mode can request a tool call during a task rather than only generate text. The tool still needs to be configured and available.
Review source

column1: The VS Code Command Palette command for adding an MCP server is {{c1::MCP: Add Server}}.
column2:
This command starts guided setup for a remote URL or a local launch command. The configuration destination determines which file and format VS Code uses.
Review source

column1: The older editor-managed workspace MCP format in VS Code uses {{c1::.vscode\mcp.json}}.
column2:
Native Copilot workspace configuration instead uses .mcp.json at the workspace root. Choose the file for the intended configuration format.
Review source

column1: In the older editor-managed .vscode\mcp.json format, server entries go under {{c1::servers}}.
column2:
Native Copilot uses mcpServers in its own configuration. Copying an entry between those files without adapting its structure can leave the server unavailable.
Review source

column1: In the unit's editor-managed VS Code format, set a remote MCP endpoint's transport type to {{c1::http}}.
column2:
The transport says how to connect. The separate URL property says which endpoint to contact.
Review source

column1: In the unit's editor-managed HTTP server definition, put the remote endpoint address in {{c1::url}}.
column2:
Use the endpoint supplied by the server publisher. This property identifies the destination, not the permission to access it.
Review source

column1: An MCP server launched by a local command can communicate through standard input and output using {{c1::stdio}}.
column2:
With stdio, the client launches or connects to a local process through its standard streams. An HTTP server instead receives requests at a network endpoint.
Review source

column1: For MCP tools that work with Azure resources beyond a single SQL database, the unit identifies {{c1::Azure MCP Server}}.
column2:
Choose the server for the service and operation you need. A SQL MCP server is a better fit when the task only needs its configured SQL entities.
Review source
